items.definition: a fenced field on a farm where animals graze
items.sentence: The horses trotted across the paddock to meet us at the gate.
items.hint: Double d in the middle, then -ock like rock.

items.definition: a small Australian animal like a little kangaroo that hops
items.sentence: A shy wallaby hopped out of the bush near our campsite.
items.hint: Double l after wa, then only one b - wal-la-by.

items.definition: an Australian tree with fluffy golden flowers
items.sentence: In spring the wattle near our fence turns bright gold.
items.hint: Double t in the middle, and it ends in -le like little.

items.definition: an Australian bird famous for its loud laughing call
items.sentence: Every morning a kookaburra laughs loudly from the gum tree outside.
items.hint: Two oo's at the start and a double r near the end.

items.definition: a large Australian fish that is popular for fishing and cooking
items.sentence: Dad finally caught a barramundi after fishing all afternoon on the river.
items.hint: Double r after ba, then one m - bar-ra-mun-di.

items.definition: a furry Australian animal that climbs trees and comes out at night
items.sentence: We heard a possum scampering across the roof late last night.
items.hint: Double s in the middle and it ends with -um.

items.definition: a flower on a tree or plant, especially in spring
items.sentence: Each pink blossom on the old tree opened in the warm sunshine.
items.hint: Double s in the middle, and it ends in -om not -um.

items.definition: very light rain that falls in tiny drops
items.sentence: A soft drizzle fell while we walked home from training.
items.hint: Double z in the middle, then -le at the end.

items.definition: a hanging bed made of cloth or net tied between two posts or trees
items.sentence: I read my book in the hammock strung between two shady trees.
items.hint: Double m in the middle, then -ock like clock.

items.definition: the soft, thick pad you sleep on in a bed
items.sentence: My new mattress is so bouncy that sleeping feels like floating.
items.hint: Double t in the middle and double s at the end.

items.definition: extremely good or wonderful
items.sentence: Our coach said we did a terrific job in the grand final.
items.hint: Double r after te, but only one f - ter-rif-ic.

items.definition: the sound of people clapping to show they enjoyed something
items.sentence: The band bowed as warm applause filled the school hall.
items.hint: Double p at the start, and it ends in -ause like pause.

items.definition: a wild snowstorm with freezing winds and heavy snow
items.sentence: The ski lifts closed when a howling blizzard swept across the slopes.
items.hint: Double z in the middle, then the -ard ending like lizard and wizard.

items.definition: a person who comes to see a place or another person
items.sentence: Each visitor to the wildlife park received a map and a sticker.
items.hint: It ends in -or, not -er - think of actor.

items.definition: a long passage inside a building with rooms along it
items.sentence: We walked quietly down the corridor towards the art rooms.
items.hint: Sound out all three o's - cor-ri-dor ends in -or.

items.definition: a moving staircase that carries people up or down
items.sentence: My little brother loves riding the escalator at the shopping centre.
items.hint: The soft ending is -ator, like in calculator.

items.definition: a small crawling creature that turns into a butterfly or moth
items.sentence: A green caterpillar munched slowly along the leaf in our garden.
items.hint: Soft er then soft ar - cat-er-pill-ar with double l.

items.definition: a crunchy green vegetable with long pale stalks
items.sentence: We spread peanut butter on crunchy celery sticks for a snack.
items.hint: Every vowel is an e - cel-er-y.

items.definition: a room or building where paintings and artworks are shown
items.sentence: Our class visited an art gallery to sketch the old paintings.
items.hint: Double l, then a soft er - gal-ler-y.

items.definition: something strange or puzzling that is hard to explain
items.sentence: The missing sports trophy was a mystery until the cleaner found it.
items.hint: The soft middle vowel is an e - mys-ter-y.

items.definition: a win in a game, battle or contest
items.sentence: The netball team celebrated their thrilling victory with a pizza night.
items.hint: The soft middle vowel is an o - vic-tor-y.

items.definition: almost the same but not exactly alike
items.sentence: Our school bags look so similar that we added bright name tags.
items.hint: It ends in -ar, not -er - sim-i-lar.

items.definition: the first one made, or completely new and different
items.sentence: Her costume design was completely original and won first prize.
items.hint: Break it up and sound out every vowel - o-rig-i-nal.

items.definition: first or most important; also the first stage of school
items.sentence: In primary school we planted a herb patch behind the classrooms.
items.hint: The hidden a is soft - pri-mar-y ends in -ary.

items.definition: the natural features of a place, like hills, trees and rivers
items.sentence: We stopped riding to admire the mountain scenery around the lake.
items.hint: Start with sce- like scene, then add a soft -ry.

items.definition: pens, pencils, paper and other things you use for writing
items.sentence: I organised my new stationery neatly into my pencil case.
items.hint: E is for envelopes - the writing supplies word uses -ery.

items.definition: good enough to be allowed or agreed to
items.sentence: The umpire said wearing sports shoes was acceptable for the carnival.
items.hint: Accept is a full word, so it takes -able.

items.definition: deserving praise and respect
items.sentence: Helping the younger students every recess is an admirable habit.
items.hint: Drop the e from admire before adding -able.

items.definition: easy to accept as true
items.sentence: His excuse about the bus was barely believable, but it was true.
items.hint: Keep i before e in the base word, then drop the e for -able.

items.definition: having the skill or power to do something
items.sentence: Our goalkeeper is capable of saving even the trickiest shots.
items.hint: Just one p, then -able - ca-pa-ble.

items.definition: cheap enough for people to buy or pay for
items.sentence: The canteen keeps its snacks affordable so everyone can buy one.
items.hint: Afford is a full word, so it takes -able.

items.definition: able to be trusted or relied on
items.sentence: Everyone wants a dependable partner for the group science project.
items.hint: Depend is a full word, so add -able.

items.definition: safe to eat
items.sentence: Our teacher showed us which bush plants are edible on our nature walk.
items.hint: There is no full word inside, so the ending is -ible.

items.definition: able to be divided evenly without a remainder
items.sentence: Numbers ending in zero are always divisible by ten.
items.hint: There is no full word inside, so the ending is -ible.

items.definition: honest, fair and deserving respect
items.sentence: Admitting the mistake straight away was the honourable thing to do.
items.hint: Australian spelling keeps -our in the base word before -able.

items.definition: clear enough to read easily
items.sentence: Please make your handwriting legible so the judges can read each entry.
items.hint: No full word inside, so it ends in -ible.

items.definition: friendly and pleasant, so people enjoy your company
items.sentence: The new student was so likeable that everyone saved her a seat.
items.hint: Australian spelling usually keeps the e - like plus -able.

items.definition: so impressive or unusual that people notice and remember it
items.sentence: Her remarkable memory means she never forgets a single line on stage.
items.hint: Remark is a full word, so simply add -able.

items.definition: special enough to remember for a long time
items.sentence: Camping under the stars made our school trip truly memorable.
items.hint: Say every syllable - mem-or-able ends in -able.

items.definition: easy to guess because it always happens the same way
items.sentence: The ending of the film was predictable, but we still cheered loudly.
items.hint: Predict is a full word, so simply add -able.

items.definition: deep sadness felt after losing someone or something special
items.sentence: The class felt real grief when the school's old gum tree fell.
items.hint: I before e when it sounds like ee - grief rhymes with leaf.

items.definition: a nutrient in food that helps your body grow strong and repair itself
items.sentence: Eggs at breakfast give you plenty of protein for a big sports day.
items.hint: This science word breaks the rule - e before i after the t.

items.definition: a type of fuel used by trucks, tractors and some cars
items.sentence: The old fishing boat's diesel engine rumbled as we left the wharf.
items.hint: I before e after the d - die-sel.

items.definition: goods carried by trucks, trains, ships or planes
items.sentence: A long train loaded with freight rattled past the crossing near school.
items.hint: Ei says ay here - it is eight with fr in front.

items.definition: a thin piece of material that covers or hides something
items.sentence: A thin veil of morning mist hung over the sleepy valley.
items.hint: When ei sounds like ay, e comes before i.

items.definition: one of the thin tubes that carry blood around your body
items.sentence: You can see a faint blue vein on the inside of your arm.
items.hint: Ei says ay here - e before i, like in veil.

items.definition: the period when a king or queen rules a country
items.sentence: Our class studied the reign of a mighty queen this term.
items.hint: Silent g - e before i, then gn like in sign.

items.definition: a sudden, high-pitched scream or cry
items.sentence: A shriek of laughter came from the trampoline in the backyard.
items.hint: I before e when it sounds like ee - shr-ie-k.

items.definition: one or the other of two people or things
items.sentence: You may sit at either end of the canoe before we push off.
items.hint: This rule-breaker puts e before i, just like its partner neither.

items.definition: a huge river of ice that moves very slowly down a mountain
items.sentence: The hikers photographed a sparkling glacier from the lookout in New Zealand.
items.hint: The c is soft and i comes before e - gla-cier.

items.definition: a group of living things of the same kind that can breed together
items.sentence: Scientists discovered a new species of beetle in the rainforest last year.
items.hint: After the soft c, i comes before e - spe-cies.

items.definition: not one and not the other of two people or things
items.sentence: In the shootout neither goalkeeper managed to stop a single shot.
items.hint: E before i in this rule-breaker, matching its partner either.

items.definition: to give way, or the amount a crop produces
items.sentence: Bike riders must yield to walkers on the shared path.
items.hint: I before e when it sounds like ee - y-ie-ld.

items.definition: able to make you very sick if you eat or touch it
items.sentence: Some brightly coloured frogs are poisonous, so admire them from a distance.
items.hint: Poison is a full word - just add -ous.

items.definition: shocking, wildly unfair or hard to believe
items.sentence: Ten dollars for one small ice cream seems outrageous to me.
items.hint: Keep the e after g so it stays soft - outrage plus -ous.

items.definition: dangerous and likely to cause harm
items.sentence: Loose gravel makes the steep track hazardous for bike riders.
items.hint: Hazard is a full word - simply add -ous.

items.definition: so silly that it makes people laugh or shake their heads
items.sentence: Our dog looks ridiculous wearing his tiny yellow raincoat.
items.hint: It comes from ridicule - drop the e and add -ous.

items.definition: having many very high, rocky peaks
items.sentence: The road wound through mountainous country on the way to the snow.
items.hint: Keep the whole word mountain, then simply add -ous.

items.definition: happening suddenly without being planned
items.sentence: The crowd broke into spontaneous cheering when the mascot started dancing.
items.hint: The ending is -eous - sound out spon-ta-ne-ous.

items.definition: spending lots of time learning and reading
items.sentence: My studious sister brings flashcards everywhere, even on holidays.
items.hint: Study swaps its y for an i, then takes -ous.

items.definition: using lots of energy and strength
items.sentence: After some vigorous stretching, the squad dived into the cool pool.
items.hint: Vigour loses its u before -ous - vig-or-ous.

items.definition: having plenty of room inside
items.sentence: The new hall is so spacious that every class fits inside easily.
items.hint: Space drops its e and takes -cious for the sh sound.

items.definition: going together peacefully or sounding pleasant together
items.sentence: Their harmonious singing drifted across the assembly hall at rehearsal.
items.hint: Harmony swaps its y for an i before -ous.

items.definition: having a pleasant, tuneful sound
items.sentence: A melodious bird call woke us softly at the campsite.
items.hint: Melody swaps its y for an i before -ous.

items.definition: very important or significant
items.sentence: Winning the state title was a momentous day for our little club.
items.hint: Moment is a full word - just add -ous, no i needed.

items.definition: giving you a better chance of success; helpful
items.sentence: Choosing the shady end of the court proved advantageous in the heat.
items.hint: Keep the e after g to keep it soft - advantage plus -ous.

items.definition: a very large amount of something
items.sentence: The orchard produced an abundance of ripe mangoes this summer.
items.hint: Think of abundant - the a in -ant stays in -ance.

items.definition: agreeing to receive something, or being included in a group
items.sentence: Her acceptance into the state swimming squad thrilled the whole family.
items.hint: Accept keeps its spelling, then add -ance with an a.

items.definition: money given regularly, or an amount you are permitted
items.sentence: He saves half his weekly allowance to buy a new cricket bat.
items.hint: Allow is a full word - add -ance with an a.

items.definition: a machine used in the home, like a kettle or toaster
items.sentence: Every kitchen appliance beeped when the power came back on.
items.hint: Double p at the start and -ance with an a at the end.

items.definition: great brightness, or amazing skill and cleverness
items.sentence: The fireworks lit the harbour with dazzling brilliance on New Year's Eve.
items.hint: Double l in the middle, then -ance with an a.

items.definition: the strength to keep going for a long time without giving up
items.sentence: Cross-country running builds the endurance you need for long bushwalks.
items.hint: Endure drops its e, then add -ance with an a.

items.definition: a pleasant, sweet smell
items.sentence: The fragrance of jasmine filled the garden on warm spring evenings.
items.hint: It ends in -ance - think of fragrant with an a.

items.definition: help and advice that shows you what to do
items.sentence: With her coach's guidance, she perfected her backstroke turn at training.
items.hint: Guide drops its e, then takes -ance.

items.definition: when two things happen together by chance in a surprising way
items.sentence: By sheer coincidence, both teachers wore the same spotted scarf today.
items.hint: It ends in -ence - co-in-ci-dence, like incident.

items.definition: the result of an action or choice
items.sentence: Missing the bus was the consequence of hitting snooze three times.
items.hint: It follows sequence - both end in -ence.

items.definition: something that makes life easier or saves you effort
items.sentence: For convenience, we keep the beach towels in a basket by the door.
items.hint: Start with convenient, then swap -ent for -ence.

items.definition: the quality of being extremely good at something
items.sentence: The academy gives an award for excellence in music every December.
items.hint: Double l in the middle and -ence at the end.

items.definition: being able to look after yourself without help from others
items.sentence: Cooking dinner once a week teaches you a little independence.
items.hint: It ends in -ence - think of independent with an e.

items.definition: liking one thing more than another
items.sentence: My preference is strawberry ice cream, but chocolate comes a close second.
items.hint: Prefer keeps one r here, then add -ence.
